why: All three checks pass, so the finding survives. Both the interval and the prompt are optional, and what you provide determines how the loop behaves." The whole two-sentence line was read; the second sentence qualifies the first, it does not reverse it. The page is row 154 of scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv, so it is a Claude contract page, not a Codex/MCP page. (2) CITED EVIDENCE ACCURATE: packages/shared/src/skills/seed.ts:41 is `export function bundledSkillSlugs(...)`, reading `getBundledAssetsDir('skills')`; `ls apps/electron/resources/skills` returns exactly `plugin-creator` and `skill-creator`, each with only SKILL.md. `grep -rain` (with -a, for the NUL-byte trap) over packages/ and apps/ for '/loop', 'loop.md' and 'ScheduleWakeup' finds no implementation — every hit is a comment or an unrelated substring (cron-tools.ts:74 '`/loop`-style polling', tool-defs.ts:1182 quoting the disable flag, loopback/loop-guard/agent-loop.md). `find` for any path matching *loop* returns nothing. Subsystem naming is correct: the doc calls /loop a bundled skill and our bundled-skill tier is the matching subsystem; the sibling slash-command subsystem (packages/shared/src/slash-commands/) ships only user-, project- and plugin-authored commands plus MCP prompts, so there is no built-in command tier either. NOT one of the nine dated owner decisions in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 (those are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries) — none touches scheduling. Not a de-brand or dropped-subscription product difference either. It is instead an OPEN, COSTED deferral, recorded in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-session-scheduling.md:163 with the category string `documented, not implemented — requires /loop, which is not in this slice` and a four-task estimate, and carried in the audit's R27 row. A costed follow-up is a real gap, not a do-not-fix decision. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE FILED STATE, neither of which refutes it: (a) the parenthetical is right that the tier exists but wrong that the plan's reason went stale afterwards — apps/electron/resources/skills and packages/shared/src/skills/seed.ts both landed in 3873459b on 2026-07-21, eight days BEFORE the plan's 2026-07-29 disposition sentence "packages/shared/src/skills/ has no built-in tier", so that half of the blocker was already inaccurate when written; (b) the plan's OTHER half is still true — there is no bundled/built-in slash-command tier — so the skills tier alone does not discharge the prerequisite, and Task 1 of the four also requires the :43 invocability gate in the scheduler delivery path. Scope note for the corrected state: the fixed-interval CONSEQUENCE is partially reachable today because CronCreate/CronList/CronDelete ship with the documented dialect, jitter, 50-cap and seven-day expiry, and the doc's own 'manage scheduled tasks' route is plain natural language to the model; Monitor also ships, which scheduled-tasks.md:72 names as the more token-efficient alternative to a dynamic loop. What is absent is the /loop entry point itself and the self-paced machinery.
correctedState: Confirmed gap, with the filed note's dating corrected. No `loop` skill, no `loop.md` reader and no `ScheduleWakeup` tool exist anywhere in packages/ or apps/ (verified with grep -a and find). The bundled-skill tier is real and populated — packages/shared/src/skills/seed.ts:41 `bundledSkillSlugs` seeds apps/electron/resources/skills/<slug>/SKILL.md — but ships only plugin-creator and skill-creator. The deferring plan (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-session-scheduling.md:174-201) gave TWO blockers: 'packages/shared/src/skills/ has no built-in tier' and no bundled slash-command tier. The first was already wrong when written — the skills tier landed 2026-07-21 in 3873459b, eight days earlier — not stale-since. The second still holds: packages/shared/src/slash-commands/ dispatches only user-, project- and plugin-authored commands plus MCP prompts. The gap is an open costed deferral (category string `documented, not implemented — requires /loop, which is not in this slice`, four tasks), not an owner decision and not a de-brand difference. Partial mitigation, worth stating so the gap is not overread: a recurring in-session prompt IS obtainable by asking the model, since CronCreate/CronList/CronDelete ship at parity, and Monitor ships as scheduled-tasks.md:72's alternative to dynamic polling; what is missing is the /loop entry point, the interval grammar, loop.md, and the self-paced mode with ScheduleWakeup and Esc-cancellation.
